chunks: And [regarding] your banner, do not let it bend down, nor leave it alone.
Do not give it to anyone except the brave and the defenders of honour among you.
For those who endure the befalling of troubles are they who surround their banners and encircle them: on both sides, behind them, and in front of them.
They do not lag behind it so that they give it over [to the enemy], nor do they go ahead of it so that they leave it alone.
Everyone should deal with his adversary and also help his comrade by his own life, and should not leave the adversary to his comrade lest both his own adversary and his comrade’s join against him.
ai.seo_question: What are the key principles of military discipline and cohesion in Imam Ali's exhortation to his followers?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha highlights the tactical and spiritual discipline of the Sahaba, emphasizing that true bravery involves steadfastly guarding the banner (rayat) without straying forward or falling back, a principle rooted in the Battle of Badr. It underscores the importance of individual accountability within the collective, ensuring that soldiers do not abandon their specific foes to avoid being overwhelmed by combined enemy forces. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of 'itqan' (excellence) in both martial conduct and spiritual resolve.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Do not let your banner bend down, nor leave it alone.
Do not give it to anyone except the brave and the defenders of honour among you
because they alone endure the befalling of troubles; they surround the banners and encircle them on both sides, their rear and their front.
They do not separate from them lest they give them over (to the enemy). They do not go ahead of them lest they leave them alone.
Everyone should deal with his adversary and also help his comrade by his own life, and should not leave the adversary to his comrade lest both his own adversary and his comrade’s join against him.
